questionText:
Read the following excerpt on social stratification and answer the questions that follow:

Sociologist M.N. Srinivas introduced the concept of the 'Dominant Caste' to explain power dynamics in rural India. According to Srinivas, a caste may be said to be dominant when it yields a preponderance of numerical strength over the other castes, and when it also wields preponderant economic and political power. A large and powerful caste group can easily dominate if it is placed high in the traditional caste hierarchy, but intermediate peasant castes with significant landownership often exercise decisive local influence. In many parts of India, land reforms and adult franchise enabled intermediate peasant castes like the Jats in Punjab and Haryana, Vokkaligas and Lingayats in Karnataka, Kammas and Reddys in Andhra Pradesh, and Marathas in Maharashtra to consolidate their position as dominant castes. They mediate disputes, control village panchayats, and act as vital vote banks in democratic electoral mobilizations.
